name: Auware
summary: AI-built, audience-specific Shopify pages: it automatically generates a personalized page per buyer persona, not just landing pages but also advertorials, listicles, comparison pages and product (PDP) pages, with targeted headlines, social proof and FAQs, plus per-segment analytics. Built to lift ad conversion for DTC brands. No code.
best_for: Shopify stores running segmented paid campaigns (different personas, interests, offers) who are currently sending all that traffic to one generic page
skip_if: you're not on Shopify, you don't run audience-segmented paid ads, or you just want a flexible general-purpose page builder
honest_knock: It's deliberately narrow: Shopify-only and built around segmented paid traffic. If you send everyone to one page or don't run audience-segmented ads, the core 'a page per persona' value doesn't really kick in. It's also newer and less battle-tested than general builders like PageFly.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 28 September 2026 and again, unchanged, 28 November 2026 on auware.com/pricing and the Shopify App Store listing) One plan: Pro at $199 a month per store, where a store is one myshopify.com domain, so each store needs its own subscription. It includes a 30-day free trial, 10 active campaigns and 6 personalized audience pages per product. Influencer Pages is a $99-a-month add-on. Larger setups — unlimited stores and team members, custom campaign and audience limits, Shopify Plus — are a 'Contact Us' conversation with no published price. The Shopify listing shows the same $199 a month, charged in USD and billed every 30 days. Correction: until 28 September 2026 this field put the plan at $99 a month; $99 is the Influencer Pages add-on, and the plan was already $199 when we read the pricing page on 26 July 2026.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the Shopify app Auware on a development store: the install, the onboarding, and one campaign for The Complete Snowboard. The AI made a baseline landing page without code after about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes, and two of six suggested audience pages after about 15 clicks and about 7 to 10 minutes in all, mostly waiting. No image was generated and nothing was published, so no traffic was sent and no conversion was measured. After the campaign was left the app asked to sign in with an e-mail and a password, so no price, trial or approval screen was seen and the cancel route inside the app was not tested. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 20:03 on the clock of the session and the Shopify screen Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; after Install the app was open at about 20:05. No Shopify screen to approve a subscription appeared at the install and no card was asked. In the Shopify admin the app is called Auware AI Landing Page Builder. The admin was in English. Onboarding: the app opened outside the Shopify frame on app.auware.com/onboarding with Welcome to Auware and the store name, with Store connected, Detecting brand style and Importing products already ticked, and a checklist: Confirm your account (Continue as this account), Secure your account (Set Up 2FA or Passkey, Skip), Invite your team, Connect a review platform and Connect integrations, 0 of 5 steps done. Only the confirmation was clicked and the rest was skipped. No password and no sign-up form were shown at this point. Core action, landing pages for audiences without code: the product was The Complete Snowboard ($699.95). Steps: Choose Product; Apply a Discount (skipped, You can skip this step and continue without a discount); Marketing Strategy (Strict & Compliant, FTC-friendly copy that avoids hype, unsubstantiated claims, and regulatory risk); Customer Reviews (skipped, Connect a review platform to import reviews, with also a button Generate Reviews for test reviews); Format (Landing Page was preselected, Listicle and Testimonial Showcase said Requires Reviews). Building Your Landing Page said Estimated time: about 1m 7s, and the baseline page appeared in the editor (Not saved yet) with the headline A Snowboard Designed for Riding Down Snow-. That was about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes of waiting. The banner box said Click to add banner image and stayed empty: no image was generated. Suggest Audiences said Discovering Your Audiences and that this usually takes under a minute. It gave 6 suggestions (Seasonal Upgrade Seekers, First-Time Buyers, Mountain Trip Planners, Gift-Giving Parents, Gear Collectors and Responsible Recreational Athletes). Two were approved (2 approved): Seasonal Upgrade Seekers and First-Time Buyers. Building the Landing Page for Seasonal Upgrade Seekers said Estimated time: about 62s, and then the panel said 2 of 2 ready; the headline of the First-Time Buyers page was Your First Snowboard: Honest Information to Help You Decide. Time to the first result: a baseline page after about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes; two audience pages after about 15 clicks and about 7 to 10 minutes in all, mostly waiting for the AI to generate. These times are rough: the clock of the session ran slower than the waits seemed to be. Review & Publish: the screen Review & Publish Your Landing Pages with the button Publish to Shopify (NOT used), the campaign name Complete Snowboard - Slope Ready Landing Page, page URL slugs of /pages/aw- plus six characters for each of the three pages, the call to action options Add to Cart, Direct to Checkout, Go to URL, Run Custom Script (labelled 2FA Required) and Buy with Prime, and the text that you can export the HTML package. The HTML export was not tried. Nothing was published, so there was no change to the theme or the store, no traffic was sent and no conversion was measured. Plans and checkout: not reached. Up to and including the three generated pages no price, no trial banner and no Shopify screen to approve a subscription appeared. After the campaign was left (navigating to app.auware.com/settings/billing) the app no longer knew the session and showed Sign in to your account with an e-mail and a password field; opening the app again from the Shopify admin gave the same sign-in screen. No password was entered: a separate account or password would be needed. So no price, trial or approval screen was seen, and the dossier ($199 per maand per store, 30 dagen trial) is neither confirmed nor refuted. Cancelling: the route inside Auware was not tested because there was no access. In the Shopify admin (Settings, Apps, the row of Auware, a menu with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall) the dialog Uninstall Auware AI Landing Page Builder? said that the app can no longer be used, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; a reason is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). Not tested: publishing to Shopify and the page in the store or in a preview, the XLSX export and the HTML export, review platforms, Meta Ads, Influencer Pages, A/B tests, plans and amounts, cancelling inside the app, several stores, 2FA and the team invite. Clean up: the app was uninstalled (Settings, Apps, Uninstall, reason Testing multiple apps) and no longer appeared in the list; the campaign that was not saved in Auware lapsed with the uninstall. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: No image was generated (the banner box stayed empty); the generation was mostly waiting; the app asked to sign in with an e-mail and a password after the campaign was left, which blocked the billing page; and no price was shown in the whole flow.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Original store creation and identity check, which we did ourselves.
Publishing to Shopify and the pages in the store or in a preview, and the HTML and XLSX export.
Review platforms, Meta Ads, Influencer Pages and A/B tests.
Plans, prices, the trial and checkout.
Cancelling inside the app.
Several stores, 2FA and the team invite.

Session and source-reading date: 17 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 20:03 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.
exit_test.note: A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. The exported file was not opened, so what it contains is unverified. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the Shopify app Auware on a development store: the install, the onboarding, and one campaign for The Complete Snowboard. The AI made a baseline landing page without code after about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes, and two of six suggested audience pages after about 15 clicks and about 7 to 10 minutes in all, mostly waiting. No image was generated and nothing was published, so no traffic was sent and no conversion was measured. After the campaign was left the app asked to sign in with an e-mail and a password, so no price, trial or approval screen was seen and the cancel route inside the app was not tested. The app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 20:03 on the clock of the session and the Shopify screen Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; after Install the app was open at about 20:05. No Shopify screen to approve a subscription appeared at the install and no card was asked. In the Shopify admin the app is called Auware AI Landing Page Builder. The admin was in English. Onboarding: the app opened outside the Shopify frame on app.auware.com/onboarding with Welcome to Auware and the store name, with Store connected, Detecting brand style and Importing products already ticked, and a checklist: Confirm your account (Continue as this account), Secure your account (Set Up 2FA or Passkey, Skip), Invite your team, Connect a review platform and Connect integrations, 0 of 5 steps done. Only the confirmation was clicked and the rest was skipped. No password and no sign-up form were shown at this point. Core action, landing pages for audiences without code: the product was The Complete Snowboard ($699.95). Steps: Choose Product; Apply a Discount (skipped, You can skip this step and continue without a discount); Marketing Strategy (Strict & Compliant, FTC-friendly copy that avoids hype, unsubstantiated claims, and regulatory risk); Customer Reviews (skipped, Connect a review platform to import reviews, with also a button Generate Reviews for test reviews); Format (Landing Page was preselected, Listicle and Testimonial Showcase said Requires Reviews). Building Your Landing Page said Estimated time: about 1m 7s, and the baseline page appeared in the editor (Not saved yet) with the headline A Snowboard Designed for Riding Down Snow-. That was about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes of waiting. The banner box said Click to add banner image and stayed empty: no image was generated. Suggest Audiences said Discovering Your Audiences and that this usually takes under a minute. It gave 6 suggestions (Seasonal Upgrade Seekers, First-Time Buyers, Mountain Trip Planners, Gift-Giving Parents, Gear Collectors and Responsible Recreational Athletes). Two were approved (2 approved): Seasonal Upgrade Seekers and First-Time Buyers. Building the Landing Page for Seasonal Upgrade Seekers said Estimated time: about 62s, and then the panel said 2 of 2 ready; the headline of the First-Time Buyers page was Your First Snowboard: Honest Information to Help You Decide. Time to the first result: a baseline page after about 6 clicks and about 1.5 minutes; two audience pages after about 15 clicks and about 7 to 10 minutes in all, mostly waiting for the AI to generate. These times are rough: the clock of the session ran slower than the waits seemed to be. Review & Publish: the screen Review & Publish Your Landing Pages with the button Publish to Shopify (NOT used), the campaign name Complete Snowboard - Slope Ready Landing Page, page URL slugs of /pages/aw- plus six characters for each of the three pages, the call to action options Add to Cart, Direct to Checkout, Go to URL, Run Custom Script (labelled 2FA Required) and Buy with Prime, and the text that you can export the HTML package. The HTML export was not tried. Nothing was published, so there was no change to the theme or the store, no traffic was sent and no conversion was measured. Plans and checkout: not reached. Up to and including the three generated pages no price, no trial banner and no Shopify screen to approve a subscription appeared. After the campaign was left (navigating to app.auware.com/settings/billing) the app no longer knew the session and showed Sign in to your account with an e-mail and a password field; opening the app again from the Shopify admin gave the same sign-in screen. No password was entered: a separate account or password would be needed. So no price, trial or approval screen was seen, and the dossier ($199 per maand per store, 30 dagen trial) is neither confirmed nor refuted. Cancelling: the route inside Auware was not tested because there was no access. In the Shopify admin (Settings, Apps, the row of Auware, a menu with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall) the dialog Uninstall Auware AI Landing Page Builder? said that the app can no longer be used, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request is sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; a reason is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). Not tested: publishing to Shopify and the page in the store or in a preview, the XLSX export and the HTML export, review platforms, Meta Ads, Influencer Pages, A/B tests, plans and amounts, cancelling inside the app, several stores, 2FA and the team invite.
